name: Clean and Jerk
description: The clean and jerk is the second of the two Olympic weightlifting competition lifts, consisting of two distinct phases: the clean, which brings the bar from the floor to the front rack position on the shoulders, and the jerk, which drives the bar from the shoulders to a fully locked overhead position. It is typically the stronger of the two Olympic lifts and demands whole-body explosive power, precise technique, and excellent mobility throughout the shoulders, hips, and ankles.

execution.starting_position: Bar over mid-foot, shoulder-width clean grip (narrower than snatch), flat back, shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
execution.setup_instructions: Use bumper plates and a lifting platform. The jerk requires sufficient shoulder mobility to achieve a stable overhead catch. Warm up shoulders, hips, and ankles thoroughly.
steps: Step 1 (Clean): First pull — drive legs into the floor, keeping back angle constant and bar close.
Step 2 (Clean): Second pull — extend hips explosively as the bar passes the hip. Shrug and pull elbows high.
Step 3 (Clean): Pull under the bar and receive it in the front rack position (elbows high, bar on shoulders) in a front squat. Stand to full extension.
Step 4 (Jerk): From the front rack, take a controlled dip — bend the knees 10–15 cm, keeping the torso upright.
Step 5 (Jerk): Drive upward explosively with the legs, then drop under the bar into a split or push position with arms locked overhead. Stand to full extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Brace before the clean. Reset and re-brace in the front rack before the jerk. Exhale after the overhead lock-out.
common_mistakes: Early arm bend during the clean pull
Insufficient hip extension before the second pull
Dipping forward during the jerk dip, shifting the bar off the ideal catch position
Soft elbows in the overhead catch
safety_considerations: Requires extensive technical coaching. Never compromise the catch to avoid dropping the bar.
Use bumper plates and be prepared to bail safely.
Wrist mobility is essential for the front rack — develop it before loading the clean.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip extension on the second pull. Full overhead lockout with stable shoulder and spine in the jerk.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Maximum explosive intent throughout. The clean is typically under 2 seconds; there is a deliberate pause in the front rack before the jerk.
coaching_cues: High elbows in the rack — bar on the shoulders, not the hands
Lock out the elbows fast in the catch
